rationale: Both candidates independently surface the ground-truth's core open concern (FLASHINFER_ATTN accepting `quant` with no consumer, silently running dense) with correct, well-evidenced diagnosis, and both note the already-resolved sage-kwargs-gating issue is fixed — giving near-full recall to each. Both also independently catch a novel, plausible ring-SP bypass bug (quant not guarded the way skip_softmax is) and the stale 'Known Limitations' doc deletion, showing strong convergent grounding. Y edges ahead on precision and actionability: it verifies claims with actual executed code snippets (e.g. showing `AttentionSpec(...).backend_kwargs()` output), pins down a subtler root cause (AttnQuantSpec.enabled vs QuantConfig.enabled divergence for dtype_vo-only configs) that X only frames as a doc mismatch, and surfaces a genuinely new, high-value correctness bug (SAGE path silently changing output dtype) that neither GT nor X identified — all organized into a clear Blocking/Should-fix/Nits structure that maps directly to merge-readiness. X is comparably thorough and its evidence-quoting style is easy to audit, but its CI-gating finding is harder to verify and its report is cut off mid-finding, giving Y a slight overall edge.
